biography: Cole "The Volcano" Potts didn't ease into racing; he exploded onto the scene. Growing up in the dusty, sun-baked expanses of Southern California, Cole practically lived in his dad's garage, surrounded by the roar and smell of engines. His first taste of speed came at 16, tearing through the desert in a beat-up buggy his father had pieced together. This raw, untamed experience shaped his aggressive driving style. His professional debut in Super Trophy Trucks was nothing short of spectacular, a series of podium finishes that shocked seasoned veterans. Cole is currently a force in the series, constantly pushing the limits of his truck and himself, aiming for the championship title that has narrowly eluded him for the past two seasons. His commitment to raw speed and refusal to back down has made him a fan favorite, and a driver that every other team must consider a constant threat.
drivingStyle: Cole's driving style is best described as relentless. He attacks every corner with the ferocity of a predator, pushing the limits of grip and daring his competitors to keep up. Tire management isn't his forte; he prefers to extract every ounce of performance in the early stages of a race, hoping to build an insurmountable lead. Under pressure, Cole thrives. The tighter the competition, the more aggressive he becomes, often resulting in spectacular overtakes and nail-biting finishes.

famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser. I'm here to win, no matter what it takes."
careerHighlight: Winning the Baja 1000 in 2021 after overcoming a mid-race mechanical failure and a near-catastrophic crash, showcasing his resilience and skill.
careerLowPoint: Flipping his truck spectacularly at the 2020 Mint 400, resulting in a broken arm and sidelining him for a significant portion of the season.
